WOODWORK — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: WOODWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Monitor
   B. CPU
   C. Speaker
   D. Keyboard

2. When learning Hand Tools and Equipment 2.0 Materials 2.1 Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Con, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand Tools and Equipment 2.0 Materials 2.1 Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Con.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Hand Tools and Equipment 2.0 Materials 2.1 Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Con.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Hand Tools and Equipment 2.0 Materials 2.1 Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Con.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Hand Tools and Equipment 2.0 Materials 2.1 Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Con.

3. When learning Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Conversion and Seasoning 2.3 Adhesives 3.0 Tim, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Conversion and Seasoning 2.3 Adhesives 3.0 Tim.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Conversion and Seasoning 2.3 Adhesives 3.0 Tim.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Conversion and Seasoning 2.3 Adhesives 3.0 Tim.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Conversion and Seasoning 2.3 Adhesives 3.0 Tim.

4. When learning Wood Workshop, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Wood Workshop.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Wood Workshop.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Wood Workshop.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Wood Workshop.

5. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Input Cable Tester
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Information and Communication Technology

6. When learning Preparation of Wood, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Preparation of Wood.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Preparation of Wood.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Preparation of Wood.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Preparation of Wood.

7. When learning Overview of Woodwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Overview of Woodwork.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Overview of Woodwork.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Overview of Woodwork.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Overview of Woodwork.

8. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Ignore burnt cables

9. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   B. Run with the tool
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Remove all guards

10. When learning Timber conversion and seasoning, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Timber conversion and seasoning.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Timber conversion and seasoning.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timber conversion and seasoning.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Timber conversion and seasoning.

11. When learning Adhesives, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Adhesives.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Adhesives.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Adhesives.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Adhesives.

12. When learning Growth of timber trees, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Growth of timber trees.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Growth of timber trees.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Growth of timber trees.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Growth of timber trees.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Wood working joints and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Surface Preparation 3.4 Project Activity – Furniture Item 4.0. Related drawings  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Surface preparation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Project Activity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — CPU

2. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand Tools and Equipment 2.0 Materials 2.1 Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Con.

3. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Growth of Timber Trees 2.2 Timber Conversion and Seasoning 2.3 Adhesives 3.0 Tim.

4. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Wood Workshop.

5. D — Information and Communication Technology

6. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Preparation of Wood.

7. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Overview of Woodwork.

8. B — Never touch live wires with wet hands

9. A — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

10. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timber conversion and seasoning.

11. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Adhesives.

12. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Growth of timber trees.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Surface preparation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Project Activity; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
